reason:
The mathematics holds, and I reproduced the iid numbers: 0.5283 (SE 0.0044) against F_b at m=32, plus 0.707 and 0.905 against F_0.7 and F_0.9. The decision consequences claimed from it do not follow under real conditions.

(1) The bound does not change a plan decision. Plan §7.11 already lists 128 as a pending candidate. It justifies 128 by cost (about 1.5e7 vLLM tokens, no HF) and by simulated non-PD rates, never by a 32-pilot certificate. B1 shows the 32 counts cannot settle the m question in the narrow regime. That backs the plan's current a-priori framing. It does not single out 'adopt 128 and re-assess at 128'. Pre-specifying 256 or 512 is just as cheap (vLLM only). The plan's own simulation gives 0% quadratic non-PD at m=256. B1 itself says the 128-stage re-assessment is obstructed.

(2) 'Unattainable for ANY certificate construction' overstates the bound. Against F_b, the bound still allows a valid gamma=0.05 certificate to fire in F_a up to 52.9% of the time. The 20% figure applies only to constructions that must also be valid at two-point worlds such as F_c2. Both figures apply only at the narrow archive world. F_a is the §7.11 toy (means 0.20/0.25, reliability 0.24), not something estimated from data, so a wider real risk distribution is not covered.

(3) F_a is a boundary world, not a passing one, so the availability corollary and the 128-stage 'obstruction' mostly reflect a threshold edge effect. In B2's own table F_a has q90 width 0.135–0.149 under HC1 and fails width under CR1 at g4 (0.153). My production-code simulation (endpoint_contrast_poly_cs, 1500 reps) puts F_a's q90 at 0.145–0.160 at m=128. With question-clustered risks (Gaussian copula rho = 0.3–0.6 across the 2+2 prefixes, CR1 by question, as the real G6 uses), g4 gives 0.157 and 0.160, both failing. The obstructing worlds F_0.9 and F_0.8 miss the same 0.15 threshold by under 0.04. Any threshold rule is obstructed by near-boundary worlds, so the error sums of 0.77 and 0.55 measure closeness to the threshold, not a real barrier.

(4) Preconditions checked against the real pipeline. A1 holds: §7.11/§7.2b select on y_2 text and e_2=0, never on counts. A2 fails: prefixes are clustered by question, and type-1 and type-2 h_3 come from shared frontier questions. The derivation says positive within-question dependence 'can only make' the argument more pessimistic. Within the matched-rho family I tested, that is wrong: the NP minimum for F_a vs F_b at m=32 falls from 0.528 (rho=0) to 0.503, 0.472 and 0.416 (rho=0.3, 0.6, 0.9). The worlds become more separable, though the qualitative 32-stage result survives (TV at most about 0.59). A3 overstates: the real pipeline also has G0.8 data, 200 A3 h_3 with 2x128 α=0 continuations. That set was selected differently and is scored on e_3 only, so it is only partial extra information. The m_i may also differ through judge failures (a minor point).

(5) The '0.569 archive constant' correction concerns the r4 problem-phase check2c number. The value does not appear in the goal archive or the plan.
fix: Restate the consequence as follows. In the iid narrow-Beta model, no rule on the 200 counts at m=32 that is valid at F_b (gamma=0.05) fires at F_a more than 53% of the time. The limit is 20% if the rule must also cover two-point worlds. So the 32-pilot cannot decide the m question, and m must be pre-specified on cost and robustness grounds. That agrees with the existing §7.11 'candidate' text, and B1 does not choose between 128, 256 and 512. Either drop the 128-stage F_0.9/F_0.8 'obstruction' or report it as distance to the tolerance boundary, noting that F_a itself sits at q90 ≈ 0.15 (0.145–0.160 under CR1 and clustering). Delete 'positive dependence can only make it more pessimistic'. Under matched-rho question clustering the pair is more separable (0.416 at rho=0.9), and with rho unknown the sign is undetermined. State plainly that the clustered real G6 (CR1 by question) is outside the claim. Remove 'archive constant must be corrected' as a plan consequence.
strongest_attack_tried: I re-ran the LR-test NP minimum under question-clustered risks: Gaussian copula across the 2+2 prefixes of each of 50 questions, Beta marginals unchanged, rho in {0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9}, m=32, 20000 pilots per side. I also re-ran the production degree-2 corrected-score test at (200,128) with clustered risks, CR1 by question, for g1 and g4. That checks whether the 'passing world' F_a actually passes under real clustering. It is on or over the 0.15 q90 boundary, at 0.157–0.160 for g4 with rho=0.3–0.6.
